identity.title: LVSM: A Large View Synthesis Model with Minimal 3D Inductive Bias

problem.claim: Develop a scalable, generalizable method for novel view synthesis from sparse-view inputs.

contributions.claim: LVSM provides encoder-decoder and decoder-only transformer architectures for novel view synthesis, using learned latent tokens or direct image-to-image mapping.
Both variants remove explicit 3D representations and 3D-specific network designs in favor of a fully data-driven approach.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LVSM by pursuing large-scale view synthesis with minimal 3D inductive bias, including a decoder-only design without an intermediate scene representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that decoder-only LVSM provides higher quality, scalability, and zero-shot generalization than prior state-of-the-art methods, with gains of 1.5–3.5 dB PSNR.
Across multiple datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art quality for both variants, including strong performance with 1–2 GPUs.
The authors report faster inference for the encoder-decoder model, attributed to its independent latent representation.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper targets scalable and generalizable sparse-view novel view synthesis.
It introduces encoder-decoder and decoder-only LVSM variants with different uses of intermediate scene representations.
Both variants avoid prior 3D representations and 3D-specific architectural biases.
The encoder-decoder variant is reported as faster, while the decoder-only variant is reported as stronger in quality, scalability, and zero-shot generalization.
Multi-dataset evaluations report state-of-the-art quality and strong performance under limited GPU resources.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly presents complementary tradeoffs: encoder-decoder LVSM favors inference speed, whereas decoder-only LVSM favors quality, scalability, and zero-shot generalization.

lessons.interpretation: Separating model variants by operational tradeoffs makes architectural choices easier to evaluate against deployment goals.
lessons.application: When proposing related architectures, state the specific advantage and cost of each variant and connect them to distinct use conditions.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when variants have no clearly reported, condition-dependent differences.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, baseline identities, evaluation protocols, or whether the reported PSNR gains are statistically tested.
The reported resource advantage is not quantified beyond the 1–2 GPU setting.
The abstract does not establish priority or independently verify the authors’ novelty and performance claims.
